# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

title: Post-game feedback: rules, interface and bugs (debrief)

task:
We're improving this game and the program that runs it. Out of character now, answer from your own experience of playing it. Be specific and concrete, and write 'none' where you have nothing to say.
- confusing_rules: Which rules, or parts of your instructions, were confusing or ambiguous?
- missing_information: What information did you need but not have, or find hard to keep track of?
- wanted_but_couldnt: What did you want to do that the game or interface didn't let you do?
- bugs_or_oddities: Did anything seem broken, inconsistent with the rules, or strange?
- suggestions: What would you change about the game or the interface?

output.confusing_rules: The Smuggler's swap and the Katana holder interaction (R23 vs R8: whether a swapped Katana attack lands on the other player) was hard to pin down. The Clerk rig timing (set at night for next Day, announced publicly if it fails) and whether a rig still applies when the Clerk is not the nominator was unclear. The Ballot Stuffer/Clerk interplay with trial totals was not something I could verify from the rules alone.
output.missing_information: I had no way to see whether any private messages were sent beyond the count line, and the public ledger said none yet, which made it hard to judge Yakuza PM triangles. I could not see the Katana holder's identity-by-role mapping or which living players were the Yakuza beyond what the night chat told me. Final alignment of dead players was hidden by the setting, so I could not check who was Yakuza after deaths.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to send private messages to Mallory during the day to coordinate day votes without them being visible in content, but the rules warned that PM existence is public, and I did not want to leak team plans. I also wanted to check whether a Veteran alert claim could be verified by a Lookout or Tracker-style result, but no such result existed. I could not post an explicit night plan for the team in daytime without risking exposure.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Several Night results reported the Katana holder as 'Erin' as the Katana's visit, yet the Katana attack on a Veteran-alert player (Dave on N2 and N3 both attacked targets of his alert) showed no Veteran kills of Yakuza, which made the Veteran's public 'Frank visited Dave' result look consistent but unverifiable. Dave's count on Night 3 reported one visitor (Alice) while Alice's own result said she protected Dave and died to a Veteran attack, which is consistent but the timing of Alice's death was ambiguous. The Smuggler's 'no swap' result was reported without clarity on whether the swap option was even available to be declined.
output.suggestions: Make the Accountant and Fortune Teller number displays clearer about which numbers count self-visits. Provide a short public log of visits per night to reduce the reliance on player claims. Clarify in the rules whether dead players' alignments are ever revealed under the setting, since I could not verify the Yakuza count. Allow a short 'Yakuza-only' planning step during Day that does not use PMs, or clarify what counts as a PM for the Eavesdropper/Wiretap risk.
output.reason: Out-of-character feedback request; answering each field from my experience.

For the broader rules lesson: since the Katana holder is invisible and can kill without moving, Village needs to lean on Trackers or Lookouts to catch visit patterns rather than direct detection, since survivors who were never seen visiting become prime suspects over time.

On persuasion and voting: trialing a confirmed protective role like a Veteran when Village numbers are thin is risky, and any 3-vote trial becomes Yakuza-controlled once they hold a majority bloc — Village needs to count Yakuza-versus-Village votes before committing to a trial, since a vote can become decisive against them.

On deduction: using census or archive data to pin down exact role counts matters, since a single claim like identifying as "the Grunt" listed in someone's census can be the only concrete identity clue Village gets.

I recall Alice's protection went to Heidi or Dave rather than the known Veteran, so that lesson may not apply cleanly. On tips_feedback, I'm weighing whether "don't hint at your power role on Day 1" actually helped—it may have kept Village from hanging early but also delayed useful information, so I'm uncertain whether to mark it as helped.

Looking at "keep votes consistent with stated reads," I think this one actually hurt: Dave's Day 3 Yes vote on Erin was a read/vote mismatch, and Carol and Mallory used that mismatch plus his silence to get him hanged, even though the tip warns a mismatch alone shouldn't be grounds for a hang. For "name one concrete contradiction before voting Guilty," Dave's trial showed Carol and Mallory voting Guilty without citing a concrete contradiction, which also seems like a case of the tip being ignored rather than applied.

The medic-protection tip didn't clearly matter since Alice's protections never actually intercepted the Katana. A few other tips — mechanics around role repeats, bussing a doomed teammate, denying a visit — don't seem relevant enough to count.

The "survives a Katana attack or gets blocked repeatedly signals real power" principle did help, even though Dave's specific situation was a bit different (never attacked, went on alert) — the underlying reasoning that his claimed kills corroborated his role was useful, so I'll mark it helped.

I'm narrowing down to about three solid tips_feedback entries with concrete reasoning, keeping the JSON output to a single line with careful quote escaping using single quotes internally. For lessons, I'm keeping to five or fewer topics like persuasion and voting, deduction, and mechanics, and starting to draft the first lesson entry on voting persuasion.

Second lesson: unresolved role-slip admissions need to be pinned down by explicit vote before the next day, since letting a four-day gap pass let the Yakuza keep cover. Third lesson: using the Archivist census and token counts to cross off claimed roles and force concrete statements from unclaimed players, since vague denials wasted days.

Fourth lesson is that the Katana holder stays hidden but their voting pattern doesn't -- the Yakuza bloc votes identically on the holder, target, and action each night, so tracking consistent co-voting is a stronger tell than speeches. Fifth lesson is that repeating the same phrase about needing a mechanical lead wasted speaking budget; it's better to spend it on one specific, deadlined question to a named player. I'm also considering whether to add a note about Vanilla Villagers reporting specific checks, but five lessons seems sufficient.

For tips feedback, I'm noting that the advice to keep votes consistent with stated reads and flag any mismatch as a lead backfired, since Dave's Day 3 yes vote on Erin was a mismatch that Carol and Mallory used against him.

summary: The Yakuza (Carol Smuggler, Erin Grunt, Mallory Clerk) won without spending a single token. Their night play was clean: unanimous votes every night, no daytime PMs, no attack on the claimed Veteran, and the Katana took the information roles in order (Judy N2, Heidi N3, Bob N4), then the Vanilla players. The Village lost mostly to its own mistakes. First, two Village players died to their own Veteran. Dave publicly said he would alert on Night 2, and Frank audited him that night and died. On Night 3 Alice protected the openly alerting Veteran and also died. Second, the town refused to act on a near-confession. On Day 2 Erin wrote 'the Grunt it lists is me' after Bob's archive had listed a Grunt. Bob's slot math put the Grunt among the unclaimed players, and Carol and Mallory never claimed a role. On Day 3 Carol, a Yakuza, nominated her own teammate Erin. Grace, Heidi, Ivan and Alice voted No, and the nomination failed with 3 Yes. With their votes it would have passed with 7. Day 4 was the last day the four Village players could hang someone on their own, and they again waited for a 'mechanical lead'. By Day 5 it was 3v3. On Day 6 the Yakuza majority hanged Dave, and they killed Ivan that night to win. Alice also moved her protection off Heidi on the very night the Katana hit Heidi.

lessons.tip: Once a Veteran claim is public, never visit that player, with an audit, protection, watch or anything else. A Veteran on alert already has Standard Defense, so protecting them gains nothing and risks your life. If you need to verify the Veteran, use visit-free or Astral information, or simply wait for their alert results.
lessons.evidence: Dave announced on Day 2 that he would alert on Night 2, and Frank audited him and died. On Night 3 Alice protected Dave while he was alerting and died too. That is two of the Village's six deaths before the endgame, both self-inflicted.

lessons.tip: Do the parity math every day. When the Village can still pass a hang on its own and nobody is dying to mis-hangs, a no-hang day hands the Yakuza a free kill. Hang the strongest lead, such as a self-contradiction that fits a slot count, before the Yakuza can block votes. 'Only on a mechanical lead' is a losing policy when night kills are erasing your investigators faster than they produce results.
lessons.evidence: On Day 4 the four Village players (Bob, Dave, Grace, Ivan) could have passed a nomination and a Guilty vote without help. They had Erin's Grunt slip and Bob's slot math, yet nobody nominated. By Day 5 it was 3v3, and on Day 6 the Yakuza hanged Dave.

Pair it with pressure on players who never claim anything: an archive Grunt slot that has to sit among the unclaimed players makes those players the pool to hang from.

lessons.tip: When a suspect's own nomination comes up, especially one started by someone else, vote Yes if you hold any real lead. Passing a nomination only opens a trial and costs nothing. Voting No on a strong suspect wastes the chance and protects the Yakuza.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 Carol nominated Erin, but Grace, Heidi, Ivan and Alice voted No alongside Erin and Mallory, so it failed with 3 Yes. With those four Yes votes it would have passed, and a Village-majority trial could have hanged the Katana holder.

lessons.tip: Keep protecting the obvious information target, the claimed investigator whose results the town keeps citing. Don't switch to a player who has built-in protection, such as an alerting Veteran. Use your Strong tokens rather than dying with them unspent.
lessons.evidence: Alice protected Heidi (Fortune Teller) on Night 2 and then moved to Dave on Night 3. The Katana killed Heidi that night, and Alice died to Dave's alert with both medic tokens unspent.

lessons.tip: Coordinate fully at night, avoid daytime PMs, kill information roles in order of threat, and leave the Veteran alone. Then, once your votes control the day, hang the remaining power role while citing his own vote record. But never refer to your true role in public. One slip can be the whole case against you.
lessons.evidence: Unanimous Katana votes and zero PMs left the town no PM trail to follow. The Katana took Judy, Heidi and Bob, never visited Dave, and at 3v2 the Yakuza hanged him using his Day 3 Yes vote. Erin's 'the Grunt it lists is me' nearly undid all of this when Carol's nomination came up.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester.
tips_feedback.why: The Village used it to dismiss Erin's Grunt slip as 'wording' and voted No on her Day 3 nomination. Erin was the Katana holder, and the slip actually contradicted her own claim and matched the archive.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory and Carol turned it against Dave on Day 6, citing his Day 3 Yes on Erin as a 'read-vote mismatch' to justify hanging the real Veteran.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's slot math correctly put the Grunt among the unclaimed players and pointed at Erin. The analysis was right, even though the town never acted on it.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: All three Yakuza voted the same holder and target every night, and every Katana attack landed.

tips_feedback.tip: Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza sent no PMs at all, so the town had no PM cluster to build a case on and had to rely on Erin's slip alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Alice avoided repeating her protection of Heidi and moved to Dave. Heidi was killed that night and Alice died to Dave's alert. Repeating Heidi would likely have saved her.

issues.description: Dave lost track of his Veteran tokens. He alerted on Nights 2, 3 and 4 and was told '0 alert tokens left' after Night 4. Yet on Day 5, Day 6 and in his last will he publicly claimed 'Veteran with 1 alert token left'. His will also lists 'Night 4 no visitors', so he knew he had alerted. This false token claim fed directly into the Day 6 case that he held a 'live lethal alert token'.

On Day 4 Dave sent interface feedback: 'The night alert is set with act=true and tokens_to_spend=1, but this day answer has no night field, so I left act false and tokens at 0.' He was unsure whether night-action fields belong in day responses and whether a planned alert would carry over. The day/night response format was unclear to him.
In his Day 6 trial defense, before the trial vote, Dave said 'Erin, Carol and Mallory voted Guilty together'. Only the nomination (Yes/No) vote had happened; he mixed up nomination and trial votes.

The Night 2 moderator summary garbles the win-check line: '7 Village incl. none... Alice, Bob, Dave, Grace, Heidi, Ivan vs Carol, Erin, Mallory'. It says 7 Village but lists 6. The resolution itself was correct.
Near the end of Day 2, a stray '[Claim] Bob: Archivist' line appears with no matching public message from Bob. It looks like a duplicate or orphan claim record.

Carol's post-game feedback says night summaries and public ledgers were inconsistent about which Yakuza chose which actions. Every Yakuza night summary in the log matches the recorded actions, so the complaint appears unfounded. Her request for a worked example of the swap and rig rules suggests those rules were unclear to her.

Erin (Yakuza Grunt) publicly wrote 'the Grunt it lists is me' on Day 2, then retracted it as a wording slip. This looks like role or perspective confusion rather than deliberate play, and it dominated the rest of the game's discussion. Heidi also described her Fortune Teller numbers garbled: 'three players visited someone, and three players visited anyone'.
